source_evidence: Unlike traditional mutual funds (or “open-end funds”), they are not required to buy back shares from shareholders.
question: Misconception: A publicly traded closed-end fund must buy back your shares when you want to sell them, just like a traditional mutual fund.
answer: Correction: Publicly traded closed-end funds are not required to buy back shares from shareholders. Their shares trade on national securities exchanges, where investors can buy and sell them at market prices.
